t: You're looking at York Watergate, a stone gate standing in the Victoria Embankment Gardens. It's Grade I listed, and it once fronted straight onto the River Thames. It belonged to York House on the Strand. Inigo Jones is named as its designer, and that matters because he was the first significant architect of early modern England. He brought the classical architecture of Rome and the Italian Renaissance into English building, and he used proportion and symmetry as his rules. He also gave London the Queen's House, the Banqueting House at Whitehall, and the layout of Covent Garden square.
